subject: food-technology
title: Functions of Ingredients: Application
welcome_lead: Apply egg, liquid and salt functions to real recipes.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE functions of ingredients: egg, liquid, salt and their roles.
final_note: Each ingredient earns its place — or it gets swapped.

concepts.def: Holding ingredients together, e.g. egg in burgers.
Brushing egg or milk for a shiny baked finish.
Adding richness with egg, milk or butter.
Adds gas to lighten a mixture, e.g. eggs.
Adding liquid to wet flour and start gluten.
Boosts flavour and strengthens gluten network.

walkthroughs.body_html: Eggs bind burgers and fishcakes, raise sponges through whisked-in air, enrich custards and brioche, and glaze pastry for that golden shine. They are some of the most versatile ingredients in the kitchen.
Liquid hydrates flour to start gluten formation and dissolves sugar and salt. In sauces it allows gelatinisation of starches. Steam from the liquid in pastry helps puff layers apart in puff pastry.

Salt boosts flavour, balances sweetness and, in bread, strengthens the gluten network and controls yeast activity. Too little and bread tastes flat; too much and the yeast slows. About 1% salt by flour weight is typical.
